That removal-side notification does not establish that post-install resource availability and Explorer cache invalidation are correctly sequenced.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve Explorer icon resources through the confirmed upgrade transition
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Unconfirmed: Explorer may retain stale icon-resource state while an upgrade removes and reinstalls resources, or a shortcut may reference a resource that changes/disappears. Cache-reset recovery is evidence of refresh sensitivity, not proof of a missing notification.
plan: Identify one affected shortcut's target/icon resource basename, installation scope and exact before/after release pair without collecting personal paths.
Reproduce that upgrade in a disposable test profile and compare resource existence, shortcut icon location and Explorer state before removal, after removal and after final registration.
Trace existing SHChangeNotify timing; if a stale-cache transition is confirmed, notify at the correct completed-install boundary or preserve stable resource identity as appropriate.
Do not implement blanket cache deletion or terminate Explorer as a default fix; protect unrelated application icons and rollback/uninstall behavior.
Add regression coverage for the confirmed upgrade path and per-user/per-machine controls.
verification: Affected icons remain correct after upgrade, Explorer reopen and sign-in.
Unrelated application shortcuts, uninstall/rollback and installation scopes are unaffected.
The fix works without manual icon-cache deletion.

confidence.rationale: Recovery plus update recurrence implicates resource/cache sequencing, and source confirms an existing removal-side notification. The resource and failing upgrade phase are unknown, so a specific code fix would be speculative.

known_information: The original screenshot and ZIP are already supplied.

inferences: Resource/cache invalidation is plausible, but it is not yet clear whether PowerToys-only or unrelated shortcut resources are affected.
issue_context.analysis: This is not resolved by the first workaround confirmation. Targeted shortcut identity and install scope materially constrain a safe upgrade reproduction; another generic archive and broad cache-deletion advice are not justified.

comment.body:
Thanks for the screenshot and ZIP, and for testing the icon-cache reset. Your later comment says the next update made the icons generic again, so the earlier recovery does not establish a lasting fix.

Could you please share these specific details if it still occurs?
1. The PowerToys release before and after the failing update, and whether only PowerToys shortcuts or also unrelated application shortcuts lose icons. If it no longer occurs, please state the working release instead.
2. A cropped view of one affected icon and, if shortcut properties show it, only the target/icon resource file basename and icon index. Please redact usernames and personal/company paths and do not upload the shortcut itself. This distinguishes a disappeared resource from a stale cached icon.
3. Whether this is a per-user or all-users installation and whether auto-update or a manually launched installer performed the upgrade. This lets maintainers reproduce the correct resource/notification sequence without another generic capture or repeated cache-reset advice.
